title: Potential unsafe C string API usage
description: The native library imports C string functions that do not bound their writes. Their presence is an indicator, not proof of a vulnerability; exploitability depends on whether attacker-controlled, unbounded input reaches them.
remediation: Prefer bounded equivalents (strlcpy/snprintf), validate lengths at trust boundaries, and review the call sites that handle external input.

title: Potential unsafe input parsing API usage
description: The library imports scanf-family parsers, which can overflow fixed buffers with unbounded %s conversions. Indicator only.
remediation: Use width-limited conversions and validate input sizes before parsing.

title: Potential command execution API usage
description: The library imports process/command execution APIs. If attacker-influenced data reaches the command string, this could enable command injection. Presence alone is an indicator.
remediation: Avoid shell execution; if unavoidable, use argument arrays with fixed executables and never pass untrusted input to a shell.

title: Insecure temporary file API usage
description: The library imports temporary-file APIs with predictable names, which are subject to race conditions. Indicator only.
remediation: Use mkstemp/mkdtemp which create files atomically with restrictive permissions.

title: Weak native cryptographic primitive indicator
description: The library imports symbols for weak or broken cryptographic primitives (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4). Their use for security purposes would be inappropriate; presence is an indicator.
remediation: Use modern primitives (SHA-256+, AES-GCM) for security-relevant operations.
